title: 3U Battery Board
notes: 4S2P battery interface using [[BQ76952|BQ76952PFBR]] with direct stack I2C_A.
[[SW1|SW1]] · Manual pack on/off switch on the battery board.
The stack can read battery voltage, current and temperature over I²C_A from the [[U1|BQ76952]].
The stack can manually command charge or discharge cutoff through the [[J9|PC/104 connector]]. Pins 39 and 40 carry BAT_CFETOFF and BAT_DFETOFF.
[[J12|J12]] · Pack output: 1-4 PACK+, 5-8 PGND
[[J10|J10]] · Deploy switch
[[J11|J11]] · Heater
[[SW2|SW2]] · BQ wake
EPS supplies the I2C pull-ups and must configure the BQ before enabling its FETs.
purpose: Connect and protect the 4S2P battery pack, with a manual pack switch and controls to monitor the battery and stop charging or discharging from the CubeSat stack.
buildEvidence: KiCad backups and the September to early October commit cluster.

title: ADCS
notes: [[U2|STM32H753ZIT6]] controller with the original [[U3|Adafruit 2472 BNO055 breakout]].
25 MHz crystal, 8 pF load · [[Y1|ECS-250-8-33B-CTN-TR]]
CAN transceiver · [[U4|TCAN332DR]]
USB ESD protection · [[U5|USBLC6-2SC6]]
The USB regulator is [[U6|TLV1117LV33DCYR]] U6. [[U7|TPS22918DBVR]] U7 ramps the USB supply to the board.
Fit one two-pin shunt on power selector [[J8|J8]]. Change the selection with all power off.
NRST test point [[TP11|TP11]] is beside SWD header [[J6|J6]].

buildEvidence: KiCad backups and the main September commit cluster.

title: Feather SAMD21 Watchdog
notes: A Feather-compatible development board based on the [[U3|ATSAMD21G18A]] microcontroller with an integrated [[WD|MAX6373]] hardware watchdog for improving system reliability.

The board retains the Adafruit Feather M0 Express footprint and pinout while incorporating [[J8|USB Type-C]] connectivity, [[U5|Li-Po battery charging]], [[U2|USB protection]], and external clock circuitry.
A [[U7|555 monostable circuit]] enables MCU power cycling, while multiple jumper options allow sections of the watchdog and reset circuitry to be enabled, disabled, or bypassed as required.
External RTC clock source · [[X1|32.768 kHz Crystal]]
purpose: Build a Feather-compatible SAMD21 development board with a hardware watchdog and MCU power cycling.
buildEvidence: KiCad backups and the main July commit cluster.

title: Magnetorquer test driver
notes: A 2 layer test board for characterizing magnetorquer coils under different operating conditions like voltage, current & temperature.
The coils are driven by a [[U1|DRV8871]] motor driver controlled by an [[U4|STM32F4]] mcu.
[[U3|INA219AID]] · High-side current and power monitor
[[U6|TJA1051T/3]] · CAN transceiver
purpose: Drive and characterize magnetorquer coils at different voltages, currents and temperatures.
buildEvidence: June commit and KiCad backup cluster, before isolated July activity.

title: 5 V buck module
notes: A compact buck converter for an 11-17 V battery supply. The same PCB supports 5 V or 3.3 V with the component values below. Normal load target: 1 A.
Input and output are on opposite short edges. Screw terminals face up; breadboard headers face down.
[[J7|J7]]: jumper 1-2 = ON, 2-3 = OFF; no jumper = OFF.
purpose: Convert the battery supply to a regulated 5 V or 3.3 V rail.
buildEvidence: The initial KiCad backup and commit cluster, before the November fabrication pass.

title: MCU-controlled solar charger
notes: This module uses an external EPS MCU through [[J7|J7]].
It contains the four-switch power stage, drivers, sensing, input reverse-current blocking, gate-bias supply and latched fault shutdown.
purpose: Prototype a four-switch solar charger controlled by an external EPS MCU.
buildEvidence: Single dated KiCad backup. Full development window is uncertain.

title: LT8491 evaluation board
notes: A single-channel MPPT buck-boost charger for a 4S battery.
It accepts two solar-panel inputs, with ideal diodes on the input and output.
The schematic and placement are available; signal routing is still in progress.
purpose: Evaluate a single-channel MPPT buck-boost charger for a 4S battery.
buildEvidence: First and last board commits available. Routing is pending.

title: 3U reaction wheel carrier
purpose: Drive four reaction wheel motors and interface with the CubeSat stack over CAN.
notes: Four [[DRV8311H|DRV8311H]] stages drive the reaction wheel motors.
The five-sheet schematic uses an external NUCLEO-H753ZI for control and four AS5047U daughterboards for shaft angle feedback.
[[J10|J10]] through [[J13|J13]] are the motor connectors.
buildEvidence: October placement review and KiCad backup.
pending: Schematic and placement are available. Routing is pending.

title: 3U solar panel board
purpose: Generate power for the 3U CubeSat using a series string of seven solar cells.
notes: Seven solar cells are connected in series.
A Schottky bypass diode sits across each cell.
A two-pin PicoBlade connector provides the panel output. The panel also includes mounting points for the coarse sun sensor.

title: First PCB · Team Anant probation
purpose: Serve as the main PCB of a simple satellite, with power regulation, current monitoring, sensor inputs, and reaction wheel control.
notes: First PCB, built during the month-long Team Anant probation.
Power regulation and distribution for the 5 V and 3.3 V rails.
[[STM32F401|STM32F401]] microcontroller with [[INA226|INA226]] rail current monitoring.
The MCU takes input from sensors and uses [[IR2101|IR2101]] gate drivers for reaction wheel control.
buildEvidence: Saved KiCad files and the submitted March assignment.

title: NRF Uno shield
notes: This Arduino shield was made for testing and learning TTC systems.
It combines both the [[u1|nRF24L01]] and [[loraRA02|LoRa RA-02]] modules on a single board, making it easy to switch between short- and long-range wireless communication during development.
The board also includes an [[INA219|INA219]] for power tracking, understanding the relation between Link-Budget and Power-Budget.
purpose: Test the nRF24L01 and LoRa RA-02 on an Arduino Uno and measure module power draw.
buildEvidence: KiCad backup cluster through the first GitHub PCB commit in April.
